title: Merceron Dynamo AI
text:
Merceron Dynamo AI

Account snapshot: Merceron Dynamo AI — programmatic personalization + RTB bidder for mid-size DSPs. Heavy emphasis on sub-50ms p95 and aggressive per-request cost targets. Interested in Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency, plus Optimize recommendations for batching/caching/quantization.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2026-01-27: Intro call (AE Sofia) — overview of Redwood capabilities; Merceron shared throughput profile (avg 400 QPS, peak 1.2k QPS).
- 2026-02-22: Technical workshop (SE Ethan) — walked through request flow, KV cache use, and current in-house batching. Fireflies: ff-2026-02-22-3472.
- 2026-03-03: Security review kickoff with Security & Compliance; shared initial answers doc. Fireflies: ff-2026-03-03-4128; drive link added.
- 2026-03-09: Smoke test of small sample workload against hosted API passed functional checks; performance numbers incomplete due to differing harness.

Use-case and requirements (customer language & notes):
- Workload: realtime personalization + bidding decisioning; mostly short-context prompts (~50 tokens) and embedding lookups for candidate re-ranking.
- Latency targets: p50 < 10ms for in-path scoring, p95 < 40ms end-to-end (including network), goal p95 <= 25ms for hot-path.
- Throughput: sustained 350-500 QPS with spikes to 1k QPS. Need predictable tail latency across spikes.
- Cost sensitivity: target reduce per-request inference cost by ~40% vs current cloud GPU infra; price elasticity important.
- Model preference: compact instruction-tuned Llama-family variants for lower compute; willing to evaluate quantized 4-bit/8-bit variants.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to smaller quantized model during contention, and region-aware routing (NA primary, EU residency for EU users).
- Caching: strong interest in prefix/KV caching for repeated user state + candidate re-rank cache; want TTLs and eviction visibility.
- Batching: need batching without blowing tail latency; seeking Redwood Optimize suggestions (batch size heuristics by request size and latency SLO).
- Quantization: pilot int8/4-bit to cut cost per token; want Redwood guidance on accuracy regressions and A/B rollout plan.

Benchmarks requested from Merceron: full-throughput perf test (p50/p90/p95), token cost breakdown, end-to-end ingress->egress latency, and failure-mode behavior under model fallback. They specifically asked for: "Can you show a 10k-query synthetic run with native KV cache enabled and quantized model variants so we can compare p95 and unit cost?"

POC plan (agreed):
- Step 1: Provide config template for Dedicated pool (GPU type options + expected concurrency).
- Step 2: Redwood runs perf bench using Merceron harness (SE to align formats).
- Step 3: Enable prefix/KV caching + two batching profiles (aggressive and latency-oriented) and quantized model variants; collect quality regressions using Merceron prompt set.
- Step 4: Joint review + cost model.

Blockers / risks called out by customer:
- Law team requires EU data residency guarantee for EU user segment before production.
- Concerns about latency spikes when batching combined with synchronous in-flight DB calls; plan to test with local stubbed DB.
- Need clear SLI/SLO definitions for canary rollouts.

Quotes / call excerpts:
- "We can't exceed 40ms p95 on our bidding path — anything above that materially hurts win-rate." — Head of Platform (Merceron).
- "If quant reduces quality, we need a clear rollback path and observability tied to prompt sets." — ML Lead.

Next steps (short):
- SE kickoff: Ethan to get benchmark harness format by 2026-03-12 (pending).
- Schedule Dedicated perf run (Redwood infra) week of 2026-03-17.
- Legal to confirm EU residency language; Redwood legal pull-in (owner Sofia).

Other notes: customer is pragmatic — will trade a small hit in generation quality for 30–50% cost reductions if A/B evals show no business metric regression. Heavy interest in Redwood Optimize automations (suggested batch sizes, cache TTLs, quantization profiles) and in per-route cost/latency dashboards to feed into their bid optimizer.
